newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zairean troops take crossroads towns - dignitaries.
newsitem.headline: Zairean troops take crossroads towns - dignitaries.

text.p: Zairean rebels and their allies have taken two strategic crossroad towns, cutting government troops in the northeastern town of Bunia off from Kisangani city to the west, local dignitaries said on Sunday.
The crossroads are at Komanda and Mambasa, both on the main road from Bunia to Kisangani, the largest city in the region.
"We last had contact with Bunia last night by radio," said Kihungu Lubono Tsongo, the magistrate in rebel-held Beni.

"They said that the town was controlled by Zairean troops. We tried to reach Bunia yesterday but were turned back at Komanda...by Banyamulenge (rebel) forces, who said it was not safe to proceed," he told Reuters.
Mustafa Lufungula, head of the Zairean Red Cross in Beni, said the Mai-Mai, a witchcraft group working for the rebels, had cut the Bunia-Kisangani road at Mambasa.

"We had teams the day before yesterday who went to Biakato (north of Beni) and found 15 dead Zairean military, and yesterday to Teturi...and then on to the Kisangani road at Mambasa, which the Mai-Mai have cut," he said.
Komanda lies 60 km (35 miles) west of Bunia and Mambasa 140 km (90 miles) west. Kisangani is another 430 km (270 miles).

Bunia is the rebels' next target on the northern front as they extend the territory they have carved out of eastern Zaire over the past seven weeks. Last week they said they had captured the town but this turned out to be premature.
Tsongo said Bunia now had a large concentration of government troops, some pushed north by the advancing rebels and some flown in as reinforcements.
"In Bunia there was one battalion of paratroops, one civil guard and one gendarmerie. Then there were reinforcements of over 400 soldiers from Kinshasa.
"Add to this all the fleeing Zairean soldiers from Goma, Butembo and Lubero, and they are all in Bunia," he said. This would make a garrison of about 5,000 men, the rebels said.
Tsongo said the Zairean soldiers had left a trail of destruction as they fled northwards.
"At the Maboya mission south of Beni they raped the Catholic sisters," he said. "These were not young women, these were old, old nuns."

"They machinegunned civilians from their trucks as they fled to Bunia, and stole, burned and looted everything in their path. Our contacts by radio with Bunia say that they are now burning down merchants' businesses in Bunia, deliberately targeting them," the magistrate added.
"This is because the Zaireans suspect the merchants of bringing in the Mai-Mai to protect them. It is also because the businessmen and the Mai-Mai are from the Nande tribe.

"The Zairean army tried to kill all the Nande in Beni but had to flee first, but our reports from Bunia say that they are now trying to eradicate all Nande from the town before they are attacked. We think many people will be killed," he said.
He said the government troops were also targeting Greek businessmen in Bunia but it was not clear why.
